title: The elephant and the mice.
lines: This is an old story from India, from the book of animal stories.
Long ago, at the edge of a big lake, there was an old, empty city.
No people lived there anymore.
The houses were empty.
Flowers grew between the stones.
But somebody did live there.
Mice!
Lots and lots of mice.
Hundreds and hundreds of little mice.
They had their holes under the old houses and between the stones.
They were happy.
They ate seeds and grains.
They played hide-and-seek in the empty houses.
And the king of the mice was a wise old mouse with a grey nose.
In the big forest next to the city lived a herd of elephants.
Big, heavy elephants, with long trunks and big ears.
The king of the elephants was the biggest of them all.
He had long white tusks.
One summer it was very hot and dry.
All the pools in the forest had dried up.
The elephants were thirsty.
Very thirsty.
Come, said the elephant king.
Let's go to the big lake, on the other side of the old city.
There's always water there.
The elephants set off.
The shortest way to the lake went right through the old city.
Boom, boom, boom!
The elephants stamped through the streets.
The ground shook.
The stones trembled.
And the mice's holes were squashed flat!
The mice squeaked.
They ran in every direction.
Some little mice were hurt.
Their homes were broken.
But the elephants didn't hear it.
They were so big and the mice were so small.
They stamped to the lake and drank.
Every day the elephants went to the lake that way.
And every day more holes were stamped flat.
The mouse king called all the mice together.
This can't go on, he said.
If it goes on like this, there'll be nothing left of us.
I'm going to talk to the elephant king.
The other mice were shocked.
He's so big!
He'll squash you flat!
But the mouse king was brave.
He went to the forest.
He climbed onto a tall stone, so the elephant could see him.
Elephant king!
he squeaked as loud as he could.
May I talk to you for a moment?
The elephant king looked down.
He saw a tiny grey mouse.
He bowed his big head.
Who are you?
he rumbled.
I'm the king of the mice, said the mouse.
We live in the old city.
Every day when you go to the lake, you stamp our homes flat.
Please, could you take a different way?
The elephant king was surprised.
We didn't know, he said.
We didn't see you.
You're so small.
I'm sorry.
From now on we'll take the path along the river.
Thank you, said the mouse king.
And if you ever need help, we will help you.
The elephant smiled.
How could a little mouse help a big elephant?
he thought.
But he didn't say anything.
He didn't want to laugh at the mouse.
From then on the elephants took the other way.
The mice were happy.
Some time later hunters came into the forest.
They wanted to catch elephants for the king of the land.
They made big, strong nets of thick rope.
They hung them between the trees.
And one day the elephant king walked into a net.
The net fell over him.
He pulled and he pushed.
But the harder he pulled, the more stuck he got.
He called for help.
A little elephant ran to the old city.
Mice!
Help!
Our king is stuck!
The mouse king called all the mice.
Come on!
Let's go and help!
Hundreds of little mice ran to the forest.
They climbed onto the net.
And they began to gnaw.
Gnaw, gnaw, gnaw.
With their sharp little teeth they gnawed through the thick ropes.
One rope, two ropes, ten ropes.
After a while there was a big hole in the net.
The elephant king stepped out.
He was free!
He looked at the little mice.
There were tears in his eyes.
Thank you, he said.
I thought a little mouse could never help a big elephant.
But I was wrong.
And from that day on the elephants and the mice were the best of friends.
Because big or small, anyone can help someone.
The end.
